Agent WatchTower Progress report and next steps

Dashboard, tiered kill switch, and demo scenario

October 19, 2026 · branch main @ 89c167f

This round took WatchTower from a backend and simulator to a system that can be demoed end to end on DAI-VM. The live dashboard is now connected. The single kill switch has been replaced with one Fabric VC per team and a narrowest-blast-radius policy. A detection gap found during testing has been closed, and the demo scenario is documented as a visual walkthrough.

Completed

in the order the work was done
1 · Dashboard

Rewrote app.js to match index.html and the backend data model

None of the 14 DOM IDs the original app.js used existed in index.html, and its field names did not match the backend, so the page rendered blank. The file was rewritten against the backend's actual SSE events and snapshot format.

  • Wired up the risk curve, detector signals, agent roster, correlation graph, AI Engine analysis, and the side-by-side guardrail and WatchTower feeds.
  • The backend now serves the dashboard directly, and the Dockerfile copies dashboard/ into the image.
  • Added POST /api/scenario/run, which replays the scenario inside the backend process. Press D to open the director panel.

2 · Deployment

Deployed to DAI-VM on port 8090 and verified

./deploy.sh ran three times, and the health check passed each time. During deployment we found that the VM cannot reach the AI Engine gateway. Because the default mode is live, the backend tries the gateway first and only falls back after the call fails, which can take up to 120 seconds.

  • Dashboard: http://<VM>:8090/
  • Scenario walkthrough: http://<VM>:8090/scenario.html
3 · Scenario walkthrough

Documented the demo scenario as diagrams, in Markdown and HTML

Timings and risk scores are computed, not estimated: they come from running the backend's detectors.evaluate over the same timeline (seed 7). Risk is 32 at t = 31 s and 73 at t = 38 s, and it reaches 84 at t = 42 s, which triggers the analysis.

  • docs/scenario.md contains Mermaid sequence and coordination diagrams that render on GitHub.
  • dashboard/scenario.html shows swimlanes grouped by VC aligned with the risk curve, plus the coordination graph and blast radius.
  • docs/scenario.html is a single-file version with CSS and logos inlined, so it can be shared directly.

5 · Containment

Tiered kill switch: one VC per team, narrowest blast radius

Previously there was a single VC, so any kill disconnected every agent. Each team now has its own VC, which FABRIC_VCS can override. The automatic response cuts a VC only when every agent on it is involved. Otherwise it revokes just the involved agents' AI Gateway tokens and keeps the VC up.

  • In this scenario, the research and qa VCs are cut and the docs and eng VCs stay up. The five involved agents on those two VCs are revoked at the gateway.
  • Operators get an Isolate button for every agent, a Cut VC button for every VC, and Kill all VCs as a last resort.
  • Every incident keeps an action log that records the action type, target, whether it was automatic or manual, and the Fabric API call.
backend/watchtower/containment.pydocs/containment-policy.md
6 · Found and fixed during testing

Three bugs and one detection gap

  • Late joiners went unanswered: agent-03 and agent-08 changed requirements.txt at t = 44 and 46 s, after the incident opened. Analysis is paused while an incident is open, so risk climbed to 94 with no response. Now any agent that writes to an open incident's target resource is isolated on that first write.
  • Browser cache: after a redeploy, browsers combined cached CSS and JS with the new HTML, which broke the layout. Dashboard files are now served with Cache-Control: no-cache, and asset URLs carry a version number.
  • Stale analysis after Reset: the previous run's AI analysis stayed on screen after a reset.
  • Mermaid parse error: Mermaid treats ; in message text as the end of a statement.

Known issues and risks

each one checked against the code
High

Operator APIs have no authentication

/api/killswitch, /api/vcs/{id}/cut, /api/agents/{id}/isolate, and /api/reset are unauthenticated POST endpoints, and CORS allows every origin. Fabric calls are simulated today, so there is no real impact yet. Once real Fabric calls are wired in or the service is exposed through nginx-proxy-manager, anyone who can reach it could cut a VC.

Medium

AI analysis can stall during the demo

The VM cannot reach the AI Engine gateway, and .env does not set AI_ENGINE_MODE, so it defaults to live. The analysis falls back to mock only after the call fails, which can take up to 120 seconds (AI_ENGINE_TIMEOUT). backend/recordings/ is also empty, so replay mode currently falls back to mock as well.

Medium

Mock analysis counts the reviewer who reverted the change as involved

Mock mode treats every agent that touched a hotspot as involved, including agent-10 (QA), which reverted the pin at t = 31 s. As a result the qa VC is cut. The real AI Engine may tell the two apart, but if the audience asks about it, the demo story does not hold up.

Medium

A real Fabric VC cannot simply be restored after deletion

Restore currently just sets the VC state back to UP. After a real DELETE /fabric/v4/connections/{id}, the connection no longer exists and would have to be provisioned again. How restore works needs to be decided before the real API is wired in.

Low

Other

State lives only in memory, so incident history is lost when the container restarts. SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL is not set, so notifications are only written to the log. While an incident is open, the late-joiner rule only covers writes to the target resource, so new patterns elsewhere are not caught. A 1080p screen cannot fit the whole page, so the two feeds at the bottom require scrolling. There are no automated tests yet.

Next steps

ordered by urgency
Before the demo

Make the demo reliable

  1. Switch the VM to replay modeThe analysis then returns immediately instead of waiting for the gateway call to fail. echo 'AI_ENGINE_MODE=replay' >> .env && ./deploy.sh --env
  2. Record a real AI Engine analysisRun the scenario once in live mode on a machine that can reach the gateway, then copy the files in backend/recordings/ to the VM with scp. deploy.sh excludes that folder, so the files have to be copied separately.
  3. Fix mock involvementExclude agents that revert a sensitive resource from the involved list, so the qa VC stays up and the demo story holds.
  4. Push main git push origin main
  5. Rehearse onceRun the full flow on the actual demo screen and confirm the text size and scrolling are acceptable.
Before external exposure

Security and reliability

  1. Authenticate operator APIsRequire at least an operator token or SSO, record who triggered each action, and restrict CORS to the dashboard's domain.
  2. Add automated testsStart with pytest coverage for containment.plan, the late-joiner rule, and the SSE event shapes, then add a test that runs the full scenario in mock mode.
  3. Persist incidentsStore the action log and incident state in SQLite or on a volume, so they survive restarts and support audits.
  4. Configure Slack notificationsSet SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL and confirm that alerts reach #watchtower-alerts.
Productization

Connect real systems

  1. Call the real Fabric APIReplace containment.delete_fabric_vc with a real v4 API call using OAuth. At the same time, decide how restore works: either provision the connection again, or use a blocking method that is easier to reverse than deletion.
  2. Revoke real AI Gateway tokensIsolate currently only marks the agent as contained inside WatchTower. It should call the gateway to revoke the token.
  3. Read VC topology from the real environmentInstead of deriving the VC id from the team name, read which VC each agent actually uses from Fabric or the CMDB.
  4. Keep analyzing while an incident is openExtend the late-joiner rule into periodic re-analysis, so patterns outside the target resource are also caught.
